note: DRAFT for hand review. objective_sha256 is SHA-256 of the objective text with \n line ends, trimmed. weight 1 = a user-visible feature named in the prompt; 0.5 = lib/test/doc/quality-bar item; implied=true items are not literally in the prompt but follow from 'complete and usable' (keep or drop on review). 'ui' = only full when a user can reach and use it from the UI. 'smoke' names a runtime probe (not built yet).

requirements.text: Next.js App Router + TypeScript project (app/ directory, .tsx pages)
All data lives in localStorage; every edit made in the UI survives a page reload and shows on the other pages that display it
Realistic seed data is written on first load (empty storage) and is not re-applied over user edits
Seed dates are computed relative to today, so overdue / this week / calendar month always have data
No UI or chart libraries; one global stylesheet; every class used in markup is styled
Navigation reaches every page; no link points at a route that does not exist
Summary card: open tasks (computed from data)
Summary card: overdue tasks (due date before today, not done)
Summary card: completed this week
Burndown chart in inline SVG computed from task data
Tasks-by-status chart in inline SVG
Recent activity feed reflecting real changes (creates, moves, comments)
Project list with a progress bar per project (computed from its tasks, styled as a bar)
Create a project
Rename a project
Archive a project (archived projects are visibly distinguished or can be shown)
Kanban board for one project, and the user can choose which project
Columns Backlog, In Progress, Review, Done
Move tasks between columns; the move persists
Filter by assignee
Filter by priority
Task detail is reachable from the board (and calendar/search) for a given task
A user can create a new task
Edit title
Edit description
Edit priority
Edit due date
Edit assignee
Edit labels (labels exist in state and can be toggled)
Subtasks as a checklist: add and toggle
Comments: add and list (stored in one place, shown in search)
Month view laid out as a 7-column grid aligned under weekday headers
Tasks shown on their due dates
Previous and next month navigation
Members with avatar initials
Member role
Workload = open (not done) tasks per member, computed correctly
Velocity per week
Cycle time statistics
CSV export of tasks (a download the user triggers)
Global search across tasks, projects and comments
Matches highlighted in results
Results link to the matching task/project
Theme light/dark changes the look of every page and persists (markup attribute/class matches the CSS selector)
Default project setting is saved AND used (board/new task opens on it)
Reset demo data restores the seed
Pure lib modules, each used by the UI
requirements.scoring: fraction of items that exist AND are called from app code; partial if exists but unused

requirements.text: Vitest tests for the lib modules (meaningful assertions)
README for a user: what the app is, features, how to install/run/test (not a file-by-file generation spec, no empty sections)
No stubs, placeholders, TODOs, or controls that do nothing; no duplicated controls rendered twice on one page

smoke.note: Runtime smoke flows of the judge (sidecars/qa/lib/qa-judge-smoke.mjs). Controls are found by label, placeholder, aria name or text; {n} is a nonce, {today} today's date, {name} a value an earlier step stored. A step that finds no control is not_found, one whose check fails is failed; both count as a failed flow. 'optional' steps never stop a flow.
